newsitem.title: USA: R.J. Reynolds says repositions Winston brand.
newsitem.headline: R.J. Reynolds says repositions Winston brand.

text.p: R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co said on Friday that it will launch a new, nationwide marketing campaign for its Winston cigarette brand.
The campaign, called the "No Bull" campaign, seeks to position Winston as an "authentic, straight-up kind of brand," said Edmund Leary, vice president of marketing for Winston.
"As part of this campaign, Winston has removed all additives from its blend for the true taste of 100-percent tobacco," Leary added.
The new product will be introduced in the next several weeks and marks the first time the Winston brand has been sold without additives, said Nat Walker, a spokesman for R.J. Reynolds.

Walker also said the product's introduction was unrelated to a recent class action settlement involving the Brooke Group and its subsidiary, the Liggett Group. Under the settlement, Liggett agreed to cooperate in prosecuting conspiracy claims against other tobacco companies.
"This is something we've had in the planning stages for several years," Walker said.
As part of the ad campaign, Winston's packages will be changed to reflect the band's 100 percent, no-additive blend, the company said in a statement.
R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co makes and manufactures cigarettes. It's major brands are Winston, Salem, Camel and Doral.
